comments.comment: This perspective is so important. So glad you shared. ♥️

I lost my son at 16 weeks and only after my D&E did I have his genetics tested. We found out then that he had Down syndrome and as a former special education teacher, I was shattered. I knew that if he would have been safe and loved and cherished by anyone it would have been me. Thank you for sharing this. It matters so so much. Addy is perfect and I wish I could have seen who my Jonah would have become. I’m certain he would have been just as beautiful!
Pro abortion and pro choice are two VERY DIFFERENT things. Saying you are pro death AND you have a child with a disability is fucking wild.

Question for the group: I see a lot of folks say they are "fiercely" pro choice but I also see the general consensus is the eugenics is bad. How does that work? You either respect the women's decision or not???----- All life is sacred, all life deserves a chance, life begins at conception----

I am 100% pro choice. 100 %!!!

I am also the mother of an adult son with Downs Syndrome. This has been a hard day for me obviously with what they’ve come out and said. But the real kicker, is that my son has been a huge fan of Jesse and the McJuggernuggets for well over ten years. I’ve spent a lot of money on his merchandise. But besides that, his family has always been so kind to us. Having items autographed for him etc.
He’s talked to my son during lives and called him out making my son son feel special. So hearing the verbiage he’s been using is rough.
This has just been hard to digest. What do i tell my son? I’m sure he’s seen the video but may not quite understand it. Can you imagine being such a huge fan of someone, and they come out and say your life is worthless? 😪🤮
You said it perfectly! Love a mommy who also experienced this in her own way
Yes! All of this. Abortion is healthcare and is not incompatable with disability justice.
I agree and thank you for speaking out! 👏I don’t have a child with Down syndrome my son is autistic and a few other things but I’m standing with you all as one community! 💛💙💛Not supporting eugenics

I’m fiercely pro-choice but have also never thought about how having better access to resources and healthcare, would actually result in LESS abortions. I’m sure the costs of healthcare, childcare, etc for children with special needs has led others to make the same decisions as them. We shouldn’t judge 😞
Let’s not abort people because they’re disabled
Eugenics 🤝 abortion.
Couldn’t agree more
Pro choice and mom of a 4yo with Down syndrome. Thank you for putting my same feelings into words.

My uncle has Down syndrome and will turn 50 next year. Because special ed was essentially nonexistent in Utah, he’s unable to read and he has really limited independence. It’s been 20 years since my grandmother underwent intensive cancer treatment and passed away. Ever since then, all the siblings have had to pull together to make sure he has a house to live in and a stable schedule where he can get to and from work and everything. There’s been a lot of sacrifice while everyone has families of their own to tend to. Over the past year, we’ve seen a sharp decline in his cognitive health that comes with erratic moods and outbursts of rage where he sometimes hurts himself or others. Now the family is faced with deciding what to do going forward for an indefinite amount of time. It’s definitely easy to make them villains, especially for the damaging rhetoric they’ve been spreading, but some people need to come down from their ivory towers and understand that providing good quality of life for someone with Down syndrome can be a multigenerational effort.

YES! Also, I think you pointed to something very important here: Of course it's important for a medical professional to provide realistic information, but news of a diagnosis in-utero is so often delivered as fully "bad." It lacks any hint of nuanced humanity. It doesn't paint a full picture. And the Ridgways didn't paint a full picture for their millions of followers, either. Thank you for speaking out both on the right to choose and against ableism.

So when IS the termination of a unborn child okay? Since you are ten toes down and it’s NOT okay for the reason of having Down syndrome which I agree, when IS it OKAY to kill an unborn baby in the womb?

If someone is genuinely unwilling or feels unable to raise a child with special needs, that's their choice. What we don't want is kids being raised by parents who resent their existence because they had no choice.

My worry is, what if the child didn’t have DS. We are seeing so many babies be diagnosed prenatal with conditions, that aren’t present when they’re born! How many make the decision to terminate (their right to!) but, the baby didnt have the condition? But yes, agree with you! Their language was shocking!
I don't know who those people are. But my first thought is that they should have said "we cannot handle this". It's not about the child at all.

I think what people are missing here is that a mother has just had to make the very difficult decision to abort her child, and we’re all bickering about it. I can’t imagine how traumatic this must be for her. And yes, I recognize they made this public, but the response they have received is from media sites picking this up to create outrage for clicks. It’s way out of scope for these people.

It was "structural issues with the face" and "Downs Syndrome is not a blessing it's objectively shitty" that got me. I could not agree more with you. It wasn't inherently about their decision, it was about their discussion of Downs that horrified me

I feel as if they assume everybody with DS has little to no autonomy, which is extremely harmful and excludes a HUGE portion of people. Creators tend to forget that plenty of people with Down syndrome frequently use the internet and can see the hurtful and offensive things people say about them over an extra chromosome.

It safe to say that no one w Down syndrome is a glitch. They are so wrong for that statement and the better outcome they are hoping for next time should be infertility because downs is honestly of so many disabilities babies are born with. Life threatening or not. Life altering or not and they are always diagnosed before birth so you will never know for sure. Don’t have babies if you can’t do whatever comes your way ❤️ a profound autism mom. Diagnosis at 1.5 yrs
